a1_dyke: The drover track runs along the dyke crest with peat water on both sides the colour of strong tea, and somebody has set sheep skulls on posts every hundred paces for reasons that are not agricultural. The hill of Kar Duhn sits on the skyline like a grey knuckle. It does not appear to get any closer for the first two hours of walking.
a1_dyke_top: The crest offers sightlines in every direction and no cover of any description, in a crosswind strong enough to make the whole company walk like drunks. Dellach observes that anything watching this stretch of moor has been watching the Ninth Sword for two solid hours. He does not develop the point, because he does not need to.
a1_dyke_low: The drove road below the bank is shin-deep and sucking, and it takes the wind off your faces at the price of everything else. The mule fights every single yard of it, Odd goes down twice, and the company buys its shelter with its legs.
a1_gibbet: There is a Warden's gibbet where the tracks cross, with a man still in it, tarred and long past complaining about the arrangement. Cut into the post below him is a mark that is not Warden work at all: a ring of nine strokes with the ninth struck through. The chisel work is recent enough that the dust is still sitting in the grooves.
a1_gibbet_mark: The mark comes out of the post in one wedge of oak, and Ilsabet turns it over twice before delivering a careful verdict. It is not a ward and it is not a curse; it is a tally. Somebody has been keeping that tally on Warden property for a considerable time.
a1_sluice: The dwarf sluice sits at the moor's throat, a channel of cut stone with its gate broken half open, and the black water shooting through the gap is loud enough that the company has to talk over it. Forty feet of the track on the far side has drowned entirely. Whatever crosses here now, crosses wet.
a1_sluice_wade: Chest-deep in water cold enough to stop a heart, with the rope line humming and Dellach's shoulders taking the strain on the far bank. Kettle counts everyone through the gap by name, twice, and the second count is the one that matters to her.
a1_sluice_round: An hour is lost going round by the reed island, and the company arrives dry to the knee and no higher, which is a bargain. From the island's high point you get the first clear view of the barrow gate, a mile off: nine lamp hooks on the arch, and every one of them occupied.
a1_sluice_ward: Salt and glass and Ilsabet's flat working voice, and the gap crusts over in grey lace that holds for something under two minutes. The company crosses entirely dry. On the far bank she sits down harder than she means to, and will not be helped up by anybody.
a1_moor: The open moor is pale tussock and black pool, with no track across it and no horizon that stays where you last put it, which is the particular kind of country that remains flat until the moment it kills you. The hill is somewhere ahead. Between here and it lies a full day of educated guesswork.
a1_moor_slow: The slow way has Kettle reading the tussocks like a page and calling each step aloud, with the company strung out behind her in single file and nobody complaining. Four miles are bought with six hours of daylight, and not one person gets wet above the knee.
a1_moor_fast: The fast way works admirably until Sten goes in to the chest, and the moor takes his spear and one boot as payment for the lesson. The company spends its entire saved hour hauling him out by the belt, and afterwards nobody suggests that the hour was ever real.
a1_moor_path: Something has cut a path through the tussocks, days old and as wide as a wagon, except that no wagon made it. Something was dragged this way in quantity, repeatedly, and the drag marks have small hard footprints on both sides of them going in one direction only.
a1_drag: The butchering ground at the path's end has been organised by somebody methodical: Warden kit stacked by type, boots in one pile and belts in another, the relief patrol's shields with the paint carefully scraped off. There is very little blood anywhere. The tidiness of the arrangement is considerably worse than the smell.
a1_drag_kit: A Warden signet and a leather dispatch case come off the top of the pile, and the case is still sealed, which is the interesting part. The seal is not a Warden seal. Nyre recognises the factor's stamp on it immediately, and her face closes like a shut account.
a1_burial: An hour of hard work in wet peat, and Nyre says the burial words properly over eleven Wardens while the company stands sweating and silent. Dellach keeps watch throughout, facing the direction the small footprints go. It costs you the last of the light and buys something that cannot be spent.
a1_ambush: Two hours flat in cold water, and then eleven minutes of violence that goes almost exactly as planned. Four Fenkin scouts lie dead along the path, and one of them is wearing a Warden's boots and a ring of nine strokes cut into bone on a thong at his throat.
a1_bog: The old peat workings have a cut face standing higher than a man, and in it, preserved down to the eyelashes, is a bog body. The hands are bound at the wrist. A strip of iron has been laid in the open mouth, deliberately, and the peat above the body has not been disturbed for a century.
a1_bog_token: Ilsabet reads the strip by lamplight with her nose an inch above the metal, and pronounces it dwarf-cut, a pay-tally, one of an original nine. The final word takes her longest to render into common speech, and when she has it she looks genuinely unhappy. It is not a number at all but a rank: the ninth hand, the one that keeps the count for the other eight.
a1_deadroad: The dwarf road runs under the hill's shoulder in a cut so straight it insults the moor on either side of it, roofed in places with slabs the size of doors. Every ninth pace there is a lamp niche cut into the wall at shoulder height. Several of the niches have been swept out recently by somebody with a brush.
a1_road_cut: In the open cut, where the sky still shows overhead, a legion milestone stands at the bend with nine notches cut beneath the imperial hand. Beside it a niche holds a clay lamp, and there is oil in the lamp, and the oil has not been standing long enough to gum.
a1_niche: The lamp is decanted into your own reservoir, and it is good clean oil, better than anything bought in Gallowmere. Kettle points out the thing you had already arrived at yourself: somebody fills these niches on a schedule, and that somebody is going to notice the level.
a1_gallery: The covered gallery is dry and dark and echoes wrong, with the roof slabs holding everywhere except the far end, where a fall has closed the way entirely. While the company stands looking at it, something in the rubble of the fall shifts once, with the sound of a chair being moved in another room.
a1_gallery_dig: An hour of moving stone by hand in the dark, with Dellach and Odd at the face and dust in every throat, until the fall gives up a gap you could get a shoulder through. A draught comes out of the gap immediately, and it smells of lamp oil and old meat in roughly equal measure.
a1_crawl: Sixty feet of crawling on your elbows with the roof riding your back, and then the space opens out into a chamber. Nine lamp niches, every one burnt dry, and nine hooks above them. Underneath the hooks a body is sitting in a good southern coat with a Ledger seal still pinned to the breast and its hands folded neatly in its lap.
a1_seal: Factor Halloway's own seal comes away in your hand, still bright. The dead man's satchel holds a fair copy of the Kar Duhn pay account, and somebody has circled the ninth signature on it twice in a southern ink that has not run despite everything.
a1_camp: The last camp is a dry hummock within sight of the barrow gate a mile off, and from here you can see nine lamps burning on nine hooks in broad daylight for nobody's benefit whatsoever. The company's mood has arrived at the specific quiet of people doing arithmetic they do not like.
a1_camp_dark: A cold camp and a full watch, and at the third hour a file of lamps comes along the dwarf road below the hummock. Nine of them, entirely unhurried. At the head of the file somebody is counting aloud in a language that appears to have considerably more numbers in it than are strictly necessary.
a1_camp_fire: One small fire in a peat pit, hot food, dry socks, and ninety minutes of genuine sleep each, which the company has needed for two days. At the end of it there is something standing at the very edge of the firelight that does not come closer and does not leave.
a1_challenge: The challenge is given in the Warden's form, three times, as the drill requires. On the third asking the shape at the fire's edge answers with a number instead of a name, and then it waits, patiently, to see whether anybody in the Ninth Sword knows what is supposed to be said next.
a1_scout: Kettle returns at dusk with a scout's report and a distinctly bad colour in her face. The gate stands open a hand's width, the nine lamps have been trimmed and tended recently, and a Warden's shield has been nailed to the post as a public notice. In the mud in front of the arch there are boot prints going in, and none whatsoever coming back out.
a1_slip: The file goes up the causeway at the third hour, and the company follows it in at forty paces, moving on the lamp-count and learning the rhythm of the thing as it goes. You arrive at the gate with the door still swinging gently from whatever went through it ahead of you.
a1_follow: Following nine lamps across a black moor at forty paces means staying close enough to hear the count, and close enough to hear one man in the file who is plainly not walking under his own management. After a quarter hour Ilsabet says the thing everybody has independently noticed. The count is not going upward. It is going round.
a1_pass_as_nine: The company falls into the file and takes up the count, with Kettle's voice steady on numbers she learned when she was eleven years old. Eleven minutes of walking in that rhythm is enough for anybody. By the end of it you understand precisely what the file is for, and what it is carrying, and to whom.
a1_night_push: Camp is struck at midnight and the last mile is walked in the dark for no better reason than the captain's impatience with waiting. The company arrives at the barrow gate grey-faced and short-tempered, with the eastern sky only just going pale behind them.
a1_approach: The last quarter mile of causeway runs to the barrow gate entirely in the open, with the arch ahead and the Warden's shield on its post catching whatever light remains. Nine lamps hang on nine hooks, freshly trimmed. In the mud in front of the arch, unmistakably, there are boot prints going in and none of them coming back out again.
a1_gate: The barrow gate of Kar Duhn is a dwarf-cut arch driven into the hillside, and its lintel carries a carving of a door held shut by nine irons. A Warden's shield has been nailed to the post with the paint scraped off it, and nine lamps burn on nine hooks in broad daylight. The great door itself stands open the width of a hand and no wider, exactly as the last dispatch described it.
a1_watch: A day spent watching a door teaches the company precisely one thing. At the ninth hour, two men in Warden cloaks that do not fit them come out through the gap, take down three of the lamps, and carry them back inside. Neither man uses his hands to open the door, and neither of them so much as glances at the moor.
e_a1_gibbet_night: It is a good dry camp in the lee of the gibbet post, genuinely out of the wind for the first time in two days of walking. At the third hour the lamps arrive along the track and stop, and a voice begins a count. It includes the sleepers by name, in the order in which they lay down, and the ninth name on the list is the captain's own.
e_a1_beam: The iron beam is wet, and the crosswind arrives in the middle of the third crossing rather than the first. The sluice takes two of the company through the gap in less time than it takes to shout a warning, and afterwards the water goes on being exactly as loud as it was before.
e_a1_swept: The rope goes in cold that stops thought before it stops the hands, and the current under the sluice turns out to be considerably deeper than it looked and to be going somewhere the dwarves cut on purpose. The moor keeps what it takes and does not make any fuss about it.
e_a1_drown: The pace is kept and the moor's second attempt succeeds where its first only made a point. A false floor of root and water puts three of the company in past the shoulder, the mule goes down and stays down, and Kar Duhn remains a grey knuckle on a horizon that nobody from the Ninth Sword ever reaches.
e_a1_fenkin_camp: The small footprints are followed home to a fen camp of roughly two hundred, which is about a hundred and ninety more than the plan accounted for. The company is taken alive, because alive is specifically what this camp is paid to deliver. A Fenkin quartermaster enters five additional marks in a tally he keeps on behalf of somebody living under the hill.
e_a1_fall: The fall is widened properly, because Dellach is right that it should be done once and done correctly. The roof above it has been holding for a century with considerable patience, and it chooses this hour to stop. Forty feet of dwarf gallery comes down in the time it takes a man to look up.
e_a1_counted: The next number is given aloud, and the thing at the edge of the firelight accepts it as a valid answer and steps into the light to complete the transaction. Whatever the Ninth Sword becomes after that is counted, and kept, and is no longer in any useful sense a company.
e_a1_kettle_alone: Kettle goes in alone at the second hour, and the gate closes to a thumb's width behind her within a minute of her passing through it. After four hours of nothing whatsoever, the company withdraws across the moor without the only person who knew the way down. That ends the contract, and something else besides.
e_a1_bram: An hour's sleep, and fen-runner arithmetic. The watch is abandoned somewhere around the second hour, and the mule goes south with what remains of the advance and all of the spare lamp oil. The company wakes in a cold camp within sight of a job it can no longer afford to attempt.
e_a1_turn_back: The sensible decision is made a mile short of the gate, and the report is written honestly, and the fee is returned in full. It is the correct call. You will spend the next nine years hearing the Rooks tell it differently in every taproom between here and the Ledger cities.
e_a1_mule: The mule is sent up the causeway alone as an experiment. Preacher walks to the gate, stops, stands there for nine full seconds, and then goes in through a gap he cannot possibly fit through. The company stands in the mud afterwards without its salt, its oil, or any remaining appetite for the arch.
